clue.text: Students about to make a mistake

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for students is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: pupils are students at school

explanation.surface: Learners are on the verge of getting something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: PUPILS read backwards gives SLIP UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip up is a phrasal verb for erring or blundering through carelessness.

clue.text: Type of paper placed face up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a clock's face is its dial

explanation.surface: A sheet of some kind of paper has been laid down with its front showing.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes to one word: laid paper is a kind of writing paper with a ribbed texture, laid means placed, and DIAL going up gives LAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid paper is a recognised writing-paper grade with fine ribbed lines, and laid is also the past participle of lay, meaning set down.

clue.text: Representation of beam in doorway

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, the beam sitting within the doorway

parts.note: a portal is a grand doorway
a beam of light is a ray

explanation.surface: A picture showing a shaft of light falling through a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction or rendering of something, as in a painting or performance.

clue.text: Less experienced coppers turned up before the outbreak of hostilities

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the whole string is flipped to read from bottom to top

parts.note: raw means inexperienced, so less experienced is rawer
coppers are pennies, abbreviated p

explanation.surface: Greener police officers have shown up just before fighting breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers looks like police but means small coins, the pennies whose symbol is p. RAWER then P, read upwards, gives PRE-WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-war describes the period preceding a conflict, the time prior to fighting starting.

clue.text: Hot peas dished out in small cafes

indicators.note: food dished out is served and scattered, so the letters of those words get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Warm peas being served in little cafes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea shops are small establishments serving drinks and light meals, which is what cafes are.

clue.text: Turning to get light lit, I spy child's toe

indicators.note: turning to suggests changing into something else, so the following letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Switching on a lamp, someone catches sight of a toddler's toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This little piggy went to market' is the nursery rhyme told while wiggling a child's toes one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: In the toe-counting nursery rhyme each digit of a young child's foot is called a little piggy.

clue.text: King George I taking a drink out for a governor of Britain

indicators.note: the drink is spread out, opened up so something else can sit in its middle

parts.note: a cola is a fizzy drink
GR is the royal cipher Georgius Rex, plus I

explanation.surface: A monarch takes a beverage away for a colonial administrator.
explanation.walkthrough: Agricola was the Roman governor of Britain in the first century, famous through his son-in-law Tacitus.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnaeus Julius Agricola ruled Roman Britain as provincial governor and campaigned into Scotland.

clue.text: Wooded area forming part of King Arthur's territory

indicators.note: forming part of says the letters needed lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across Arthur's and territory

explanation.surface: A forest within the lands of the legendary King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurst is an old word for a wooded hill or copse, surviving in many English place names.

clue.text: Executed cherub hated being bad

parts.note: a putto is a cherub figure in Renaissance art

indicators.note: something bad is wrong or spoilt, so that word's letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angel who hated being naughty was executed.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone to death is to kill them as a judicial punishment, so the past form matches executed.

clue.text: Prime Minister, democratic leader, country's first person

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a Middle Eastern country
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A list of political figures: a premier, a party leader, and a nation's foremost citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: First person is grammar, the pronoun I, not someone important.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli twice held Britain's top political office as Conservative premier in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Something curious — fish crosses river with it

indicators.note: the fish crosses, spanning over the other pieces so they end up inside it

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
R is the map abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd sight: a fish carrying something across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is an unusual object or occurrence, a curiosity seldom seen.

clue.text: Actual site for a new allotment

parts.note: real means actual
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A genuine plot of land is found for a fresh vegetable garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Allotment suggests a British garden plot, but here it means a sharing out.
explanation.definitionFit: A reallocation is a fresh distribution or assignment of resources, i.e. a new allotting.

clue.text: Ancient, as a setting for old people

indicators.note: a setting is an arrangement, so the preceding letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something archaic used as a backdrop for elderly folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Old people looks like the elderly but means a people of ancient times: the Canaanites lived in the land of Canaan in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canaanites were an ancient Semitic nation inhabiting the Levant before the Israelites.

clue.text: Infant born in a tree

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other, the birth sign sitting inside the tree

parts.note: a bay is a laurel tree
b is the abbreviation for born in records

explanation.surface: A child delivered up in the branches, as in the lullaby 'Rock-a-bye Baby'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is a very young child, which is what an infant is.

clue.text: Skilful story book editor

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor handy with a narrative volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented means gifted or able, having natural aptitude, which is close to skilful.

clue.text: Innovative form of air transport — and where the Guardian may be bought

definitions.text: where the Guardian may be bought

parts.note: innovative things are new
SST is a supersonic transport, such as Concorde
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boast about some new aircraft, tacked onto a plug for the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle ran in the Guardian, so the definition is a cheeky self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsstand is a kiosk or stall selling papers, so it is a place to buy a daily paper.

clue.text: Boys are very fond of aromatic plant

parts.note: lads are boys
to love is to be very fond of

explanation.surface: Young men adore a sweet-smelling herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lad's love is the folk name for southernwood, a fragrant shrubby wormwood grown in gardens.

clue.text: Friend left in front of shopping complex in the heart of London's clubland

parts.note: a pal is a friend
L is the abbreviation for left
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A friend left outside a shopping centre in the West End.
explanation.walkthrough: Pall Mall is a street in London's St James's, lined with famous gentlemen's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The street is home to traditional members' establishments such as the Athenaeum and Reform, making it central to clubland.

clue.text: Inventor, firstly, was always testing technology

indicators.note: firstly says to keep the opening letter of each of the next words

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An inventor was forever trying out new gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: James Watt, the Scottish engineer, improved the steam engine.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt devised the separate condenser for steam engines, so he is a famous engineer and innovator.

clue.text: Father is holding learners responsible for unnecessary embellishments

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: holding means the second part grips the learners inside it

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner driver's plate, doubled for plural

explanation.surface: A priest in charge of trainee drivers gets blamed for extra flourishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Learners are L-plate drivers in Britain, where a learner must display an L on the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Frills are decorative extras or ornamental trimmings that serve no essential purpose.

clue.text: Thirteen pass out hereabouts

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of place and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Thirteen people faint around here.
explanation.definitionFit: In these parts is an idiom meaning in this neighbourhood or locality, just as hereabouts does.

clue.text: Meat for Arab leader brought into college dining room

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing meat; the clue gives the noun

indicators.note: brought into places that letter inside the room that follows

parts.note: hall is the dining room of a college

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, the only one kept

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Food for a sheikh served in a university refectory.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside HALL: HA-L-AL. Strictly halal is an adjective, so 'Meat' is a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal meat is slaughtered and prepared according to Islamic dietary law.

clue.text: Rock and roll fanatics

indicators.note: to roll is to turn over, so the next word is flipped end to end

parts.note: nuts are enthusiasts or fanatics

explanation.surface: Fans of rock and roll music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and roll' reads as one phrase, but it splits: Rock is the definition and roll the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock someone is to shock or stagger them, which is what stun means.

clue.text: Verdi opera, say, before and after orchestral overture

indicators.note: an overture opens a piece, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: opening letter, placed before
to say is to tell
the same opening letter, placed after

explanation.surface: Introducing a Verdi opera with its orchestral prelude.
explanation.walkthrough: The single O goes both before and after TELL, giving OTELLO, Verdi's Italian spelling of Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Otello is Verdi's 1887 opera based on Shakespeare's tragedy Othello.

clue.text: Fine gentlemen annoy social workers

parts.note: to gall is to irritate
ants are social insects living in colonies, and workers are their labourer caste

explanation.surface: Smart men irritate the people from the council's welfare department.
explanation.walkthrough: Social workers sounds like a profession, but it means insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallants are dashing, fashionable men of chivalrous bearing, an old term for courtly dandies.

clue.text: Old instrument designed for rest and play

indicators.note: designed means made to a plan, so the following letters are put together anew

parts.note: the two words taken as written, without and

explanation.surface: An antique instrument made for relaxation and amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is a medieval plucked stringed instrument, an ancient zither-like device.

clue.text: Empty space in French cars

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
dans is French for in

explanation.surface: Room going spare in Gallic motor vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedans are enclosed saloon cars, the usual American name for such vehicles.
